turn2.differences: The author's three conditions (c1 team, c2 title, c3 content mention) match my step-1 reading closely. The one implicit gap is exactly the ambiguity in c1: whether a document needs teamId=t-growth directly, or whether being under a project named/linked to Growth also counts. Only d-team-f1 tests this, and a careful reading (no teamId present, only projectId) leans toward failing c1.

ambiguity_effects.explain: If this requires a direct teamId match, d-team-f1 (only has projectId=pr-growth, no teamId) fails c1. If read more loosely to include documents under a project named/linked to Growth, d-team-f1 could pass. This genuinely changes whether d-team-f1 is a match.
This affects d-title ('Draft notes v2'). A careful reader settles on requiring an exact title match, so d-title fails c2; this is a designed near-miss rather than genuine ambiguity.
